analysis.title: AI rebound provides opportunity to reduce concentrated exposures (UBS House View Daily US)
key_insights: US stocks rebounded Monday after last week's steep sell-off. S&P 500 closed +4.7%, Nasdaq 100 +6.9%, NVIDIA +31.5% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

Last week the Nasdaq fell around 10%, its largest weekly decline since March 2020, and closed Friday 19.8% below its 6 October high, near bear market territory. The S&P 500 lost 8.6% on the week and was about 11.5% below its 6 October high.

UBS does not see the volatility as a break in the structural AI investment story. Cloud growth, rising usage and compute demand remain supportive, but it expects more differentiation between platforms with visible monetization and debt-dependent or speculative names.
Investor focus has shifted from the scale of AI capex to the returns it may generate, which is driving the higher volatility.

UBS keeps global and US equities at Neutral given elevated expectations, concentrated leadership and uncertainty on AI monetization. It advises holding exposure near strategic allocation, not selling equities.

Use the rebound to cut overlapping US megacap tech positions. UBS favors the Eurozone (similar earnings growth, lower valuations, broader sector mix), industrials and health care, and US equal-weight strategies.

Within AI, favor established platforms with visible monetization, strong balance sheets and internal funding. Prefer compute, leading foundries and select semiconductor equipment. Be cautious on leveraged capacity providers and names exposed to weaker capex, normalizing prices or poor utilization.

Rebalance into fixed income at intermediate duration of roughly 2-10 years. The most compelling return potential is in select high yield and EM bonds yielding 7-8%, with greater credit risk and equity-like sensitivity.

Gold is rated Attractive with a forecast of USD 5,000/oz by December 2027. Gold fell 9% last week and rebounded 3% to USD 3,636/oz. Supports are central bank diversification, sovereign debt, geopolitics and Chinese demand. Pressures are higher real yields, dollar strength and liquidity-driven selling.
Diversified commodities including copper and macro, market-neutral and fixed income relative value hedge funds are recommended as diversifiers.

Chinese equities: MSCI China is down 11% from its early November high, while the onshore CSI 300 is down 3.6%. UBS keeps China A-shares Attractive and H-shares Neutral, preferring onshore AI-linked tech, domestic semi equipment, export leaders and non-bank financials.

Other China preferences include CDMOs, innovative drug developers, large state-owned banks for dividends, and select insurers and brokers. Internet platforms' AI monetization lags capex, and US limits on remote access to advanced chips weigh on sentiment.
Asia rallied Tuesday: Taiwan +9%, Kospi +6.3%, Nikkei 225 +3.9%. The holiday-shortened Thanksgiving week and thin liquidity may be amplifying index swings.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose 31.5% Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO, driving the broader rebound.

sector_views.rationale: Preferred at sector level to diversify away from tech concentration.
Preferred sector alongside industrials for diversification.
Reduce overlapping megacap exposure, favor quality in compute, foundries and semi equipment, cautious on leveraged capacity providers.
Rebalance toward strategic weight, favor 2-10 year maturities and select high yield and EM at 7-8% yields.
Gold Attractive with USD 5,000/oz target by Dec 2027, and diversified commodities including copper help against inflation and geopolitics.

earnings_insights: Alibaba and Tencent latest quarterly results (already reported) showed an acceleration in cloud revenue growth. Concerns remain on free cash flow and slower cloud growth next year due to constrained capacity.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasuries gave back some of last week's risk-off rally.
Small move, steepening on the day versus the 2-year.
Rebounded 3% after a 9% drop last week.
UBS sees large upside over 12+ months.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance away from US megacap tech toward Eurozone equities, industrials, health care and US equal-weight strategies
trade_ideas.rationale: Eurozone offers similar earnings growth to the US with lower valuations and broader sector mix.

trade_ideas.description: Add intermediate-duration fixed income (2-10 years) and select high yield and EM bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields give income and a cushion if yields rise, with 7-8% yields in select HY and EM.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher credit risk and equity-like sensitivity in HY and EM.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, target USD 5,000/oz by December 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank diversification, sovereign debt, geopolitics and Chinese demand support its strategic role.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher US real yields, dollar strength and liquidity-driven selling.

risk_factors: Uncertainty on AI monetization and returns on capex.
Dependence on debt, scarce capacity or speculative growth among AI companies.
Weaker capital spending, normalizing prices or disappointing utilization.
Higher US yields and uneven China recovery.
US chip access restrictions on China.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq weekly drop of about 10% was the largest since March 2020, and the index was 19.8% below its 6 October high at Friday's close.
S&P 500 fell 8.6% last week into correction territory.
Holiday-shortened week with reduced liquidity and pre-Thanksgiving adjustments may amplify index swings either direction.
Concentration in US megacap tech is the key positioning risk, with UBS advising use of strength to reduce overlap.
geopolitical: US restrictions on remote access to advanced chips weigh on Chinese equity sentiment.
Government policy is increasingly driving economic outcomes, and geopolitical uncertainty supports gold.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth, rising usage and continued demand for computing capacity remain supportive of the structural AI story.
tension_points.bear_case: Focus has shifted from capex scale to returns, with concerns about AI monetization, debt-funded capacity and free cash flow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in AI investment rates, compute demand, financing conditions or the revenue to free cash flow to investment relationship, which UBS lists as factors to watch before changing its tactical stance.
